title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a figure only, titled 'Cas IV', and belongs to the sequence in which Grothendieck works out combinatorial presentations of a fundamental groupoid. The setting is as follows. A compact oriented surface X carries a 'carte' (a dessin), described by the set R of flags/triangles r. On R act the permutations σ_0, σ_1, σ_∞, also written τ_i on the next page. One removes the vertices of types 0, 1 and ∞ to get the punctured surface X̃*. On X̃* one takes as base points the points R_r^{ij} lying on the sides of the fundamental triangles. The generating arcs are:
- a_r^i, crossing a triangle;
- λ_r^i and Λ_r^i, turning around a puncture from one side to the next.
The surrounding pages produce '4 = 1+3' presentations of Π_1(X̃*, S). The previous page eliminates the base points not on type-1 sides, which leaves relations (16), one loop per vertex R_r^{∞1}. The next page treats the remaining case(s), apparently those labelled 'Cas IV' here. There one keeps only the arcs a_r^∞ and the base points R_r^{01}, R_r^{10}. The arcs Λ_r^0 and Λ'_r^1 are half-turns around the 0- and 1-punctures. The only relations are the trivial redundancy relations Λ_r^0 Λ^0_{τ_1 r} = 1 and Λ'_r^1 Λ'^1_{τ_0 r} = 1, so the groupoid is free on the remaining arcs. The geometric reason is drawn on this page and described in the next page's caption. The surface is tiled by polygonal faces centred at the ∞-vertices, with the corners rounded off to avoid the holes. The figure draws one cell decomposition of the plane. Along a path through it, small circles carrying arrows are drawn around successive vertices (punctures) and around points on edges. These circles depict the elementary arcs that go round each hole from one adjacent base point to the next. They are chained together by the arcs crossing the cells. So the picture shows the 1-skeleton onto which the punctured surface deformation-retracts: a ribbon/fat graph made of small circles around the punctures, joined by transverse arcs. Any path in X̃* deforms into a concatenation of these elementary arcs, which is why the resulting presentation is free. The purpose is to have explicit, combinatorially canonical presentations of the fundamental groupoid of the dessin's surface, with base points tied to the map. Such presentations are what one needs to write down the Galois/Teichmüller action concretely.
errors: No mathematical statements appear on this page, so there is nothing to check. The figure is schematic and hand-drawn, and some circles and arrows are ambiguous (e.g. which circles surround punctures and which surround edge base points). Cannot be verified in detail.

ideas.what: Deformation retraction of a punctured surface carrying a map/dessin onto a graph formed by small loops around the punctures joined by transverse arcs. This gives a free presentation of the fundamental groupoid relative to a set of base points on the edges.
ideas.modern_name: ribbon graph / fat graph spine of a punctured surface; free presentation of the fundamental groupoid of a graph
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical combinatorial topology; in the dessins context Grothendieck (Esquisse, 1984), with ribbon-graph spines associated with Penner, Harer, Kontsevich
ideas.where_published: The Esquisse d'un programme discusses cartographic groups and fundamental groupoids with base points tied to the dessin, but not this specific figure.

ideas.what: Using several different sets of base points (S, or S minus the points of one type i) to obtain several presentations of the same fundamental groupoid ('4 = 1+3 presentations').
ideas.modern_name: fundamental groupoid on a set of base points (tangential/combinatorial base points)
ideas.usually_credited_to: R. Brown (groupoid van Kampen), Grothendieck (SGA1 groupoid viewpoint)
ideas.where_published: The Esquisse d'un programme advocates fundamental groupoids with multiple base points in the Teichmüller tower context.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is purely an illustration of a routine combinatorial-topology fact: a punctured surface retracts onto a graph, so its fundamental groupoid is free. It is a step in the explicit presentations developed on the adjacent pages and contains no new result or connection.
transcription_corrections: The page contains only the figure, the label 'Cas IV' and the page number 118. The figure is better described as a cell decomposition of the plane into polygonal faces (consistent with the next page's 'pavage par des faces polygonales de centre les sommets de type ∞'). On it, a chain of small arrowed circles surrounds successive punctures/vertices and edge base points, depicting the elementary arcs (Λ, λ) going around the holes.
